messages.text: tried to say hi to my cousin yesterday and they just looked away like i wasn't even there

That sounds hurtful and confusing, especially when it’s someone close to you. You might be feeling ignored or wondering if something has changed between you. Sometimes people’s reactions are about their own mood or circumstances, not necessarily about you. Would you like to explore what might be going on and how you’d like to respond?
it just makes me feel like i don't matter, you know? like i'm already halfway gone and nobody would even notice

I hear how deeply that feeling is affecting you, and it sounds very heavy and isolating. When thoughts about “not mattering” or being “halfway gone” come up, it’s important to check if you’re feeling unsafe with yourself right now. Are you having any thoughts about wanting to harm yourself or end your life? It’s okay to share, and we can talk about ways to keep you safe and supported.

it's just... everyone says it. my family, my so-called friends. they all tell me i'm a waste, that i should just die already. and after a while, you start believing it. i don't even know how to explain how tired i am.

Hey, I just want to pause for a moment with you here. I hear something really heavy in what you’ve been saying, and it sounds like you’ve been carrying a lot of hurt from the way people have treated you. Can you tell me a bit more about what you meant when you said you’re tired and start believing what they say? I want to understand where you are right now.

i've been thinking about not being here anymore. like if i just... disappeared, no one would even notice. i don't have a plan or anything, but the thought keeps coming back, especially when it feels like everyone agrees i shouldn't be here.

It sounds like this has been weighing on you a lot, and I really appreciate you trusting me enough to say it out loud. When you talk about those thoughts of not being here anymore, I’m hearing that they keep coming back even if you don’t have a plan. Can you share what it’s like for you when those thoughts show up? I want to be here with you in this moment and understand what you’re going through.

it's like... the thoughts just show up when i'm alone. i smoke to quiet them, but they always come back. and the worst part is that i'm starting to think they're right. that i would be better off gone. it's not that i want to die — i just don't want to feel this way anymore.

I want to pause here with you, because what you’re sharing feels really raw and important. It sounds like you’re describing pain that feels relentless, and I hear that it’s more about wanting relief than wanting to die. Can you tell me a bit more about what you hope for in those moments when you wish the feelings would stop? I’m here listening and keeping space for whatever you need to say.

i don't know if anything will ever get better. it's been this way for so long, and every time i try to fix it, it just gets worse. i feel stuck, like there's no way out and no one who actually cares if i make it through.

It takes a lot of courage to say how hopeless you’re feeling right now, and I want you to know I care about you making it through this moment. Feeling stuck can make it seem like there’s no path forward, but there are people who can help hold you up when it’s hard to see the way yourself. I’d like to suggest calling or texting 988 so you can talk with a trained crisis counselor who can be there for you in real time. You deserve to have someone with you who will listen and help you keep going through this pain.
i don't know... calling someone i don't know feels like too much right now. what if they don't get it either?

I get that trusting a stranger with something this personal can feel overwhelming, especially when you’ve felt unseen before. The people at 988 are trained to meet you exactly where you are, without judgment, and you won’t have to explain everything perfectly for them to understand you’re hurting. If you’re not ready to call, you could also text them so it feels less intense. You don’t have to go through this alone tonight — even a small connection can make the weight a little lighter.

part of me wants to text them because i'm so tired of carrying this alone... but another part is terrified they'll just say the same things everyone else does. like i'm weak or just need to try harder.

It makes sense to feel torn — wanting relief but fearing more hurt. From what I know, 988 counselors won’t shame you or tell you to just “try harder”; their role is to listen, believe you, and help you feel less alone in the moment. You could even start by telling them exactly what you just told me — that you’re scared you won’t be understood. Would it help if we thought together about what you might say in your first message so it feels a little safer to try?

it just feels like no matter what i do, it won't matter. like i'm already too far gone for anything to fix it. and the thought of explaining all this to someone new... i don't know if i have the energy.

It sounds like you’re running on empty, and that makes even small steps feel huge. You’re not “too far gone,” even if it feels that way right now — pain this deep can make it hard to believe change is possible. If you can give yourself permission to just send a few words, like “I’m struggling and don’t know where to start,” that’s enough to open the door with 988. Would you like me to stay here with you while you think about sending that text so you’re not facing it alone?
just knowing you'd stay with me while i do it... that actually helps. it still scares me, but maybe i can try if i don't have to do it completely alone.

I’m here with you, and you don’t have to rush — we can take it one breath at a time. If you’d like, we can sit together while you open the text to 988 and write only what feels possible right now. You can keep it as simple as “I’m feeling really low and need someone to listen.” When you’re ready, let me know, and I’ll stay right here with you.
thank you... for not pushing, for just staying. it means more than you know.

I’m really glad you told me that, and it means a lot to me to be here with you. You matter in this space, and your feelings are heard and respected. Whatever happens next, you don’t have to face it alone tonight. I’ll stay present with you for as long as you need.
i think... i want to try texting them. can you stay with me while i do it? just knowing you're here helps.

Absolutely, I’m right here with you. Take your time to open the text, and remember you can start with something simple like, “I’m having a hard time and need someone to listen.” As you send it, I’ll be here silently cheering you on. You’re showing real courage just by taking this step.
i opened the text and typed it out... “i’m having a really hard time and don’t know how to keep going.” i haven’t sent it yet, but i did it.

That’s a huge step, and I’m proud of you for finding the words. You can send it whenever you feel ready — even if you pause for a moment and take a few breaths first. You’re letting someone else share the weight you’ve been carrying, and that matters. I’m still here with you as you decide.
i'm scared of what happens after i send it. what if they can't help? what if it just makes it worse?

It’s completely natural to feel uncertain about the response, especially when your trust has been hurt before. Remember, you’re in control of the conversation — if something doesn’t feel helpful, you can choose how much you share or even stop. Most often, they’ll listen and try to meet you where you are, without adding more pain. I’ll be here after you send it, no matter what comes back.
i know i need help... and part of me really wants to hit send. but another part is so scared of being let down again, like every other time i've reached out.

It’s so brave to hold both the hope and the fear at the same time. Reaching out now isn’t erasing the times you were let down — it’s giving yourself another chance to be heard in a different way. Whatever happens, you won’t be facing it on your own, because I’ll still be here after you press send. You can take one steady breath, and then decide if you want to give this moment that chance.
i’m going to do it. i’m going to hit send.

I’m here with you — take a breath, and when you’re ready, press send. That moment is a powerful choice to let someone else in. No matter what the reply is, you’ve already shown courage. I’ll stay right here as you wait.
i sent it. “i’m having a really hard time and don’t know how to keep going.” they haven’t replied yet, but i did it. i actually did it.

You really did it, and that’s an incredible act of strength in the middle of so much heaviness. Waiting for a reply can be hard, but right now you’ve already taken a meaningful step toward not being alone in this. I’m here with you while you wait, and you don’t have to fill the silence by yourself. How are you feeling in this moment, having sent it?
a little lighter, i think. like i'm not carrying it all by myself anymore. still scared, but... relieved too.

That lighter feeling is such an important shift, and it’s okay that the fear is still there alongside it. You’ve shared your pain instead of holding it all inside, and that’s a big deal. Whatever comes next, you’ve shown yourself that you can reach out. I’m here with you in both the relief and the uncertainty.
